# Independent audit: left-quantile convex obstacle

Audited source:
`candidate b12ff19e04f5fad1`,
Sections1--6. Full mathematical read: PASS. No repair identified. This
audit treats the archived projective-energy joint concavity, the finite
fixed-matrix feasible-slope bound, and whole-fiber capture lemma as stated
dependencies, while checking their application here.

Reran `supporting computation verify_left_quantile_obstacle_slab_recovery.py`: 120,489 exact
calibration checks PASS. These supplement the analytic audit and do not
replace its general quantile-attainment and convexity arguments.

## 1. Quantiles, clamping, and attainment

For a nonzero continuous normal every sampled fiber gives an absolutely
continuous one-dimensional projection, so the full tail is continuous.
Its Q-level is a compact interval, and the two weak-inequality equivalences
in Section1 use exactly its left and right endpoints as stated.

At fixed real base z, the status-clamping system has fixed row vectors
+/-(p-z). Proper cuts impose equalities with bounded right sides;
full/empty cuts impose one-sided constraints, also bounded. A minimum-norm
feasible solution is bounded by the finitely many independent active-row
systems. Dependent or zero rows cause no difficulty because the original
tilt is feasible. Supporting traces have zero d-volume, so classifying
them by full/empty VOLUME preserves actual closed-cap mass. Keeping u on
its norm sphere prevents loss of volume continuity in the compact limit.

For the signed-radius supremum, the clamped cap retains both mass Q and
its chosen margin. At the limit its actual left quantile may move left,
which can only increase the margin. The defining supremum gives the
reverse inequality; thus the attained margin is exactly the supremum.
This is sufficient even at a nontrivial projection gap. It correctly
does not assert a uniform tilt bound while the real source base varies.

## 2. Exact atomic domain and scalar equivalence

When base depth>Q, the closed nonnegative base-margin group has total
mass>Q. The common lower continuous support bound therefore puts its
left Q-quantile strictly above the stated test threshold. Compactness of
the continuous unit sphere gives the claimed finite upper bound on r_Q.

When a closed atomic halfspace has mass<=Q, its excluded bases have a
strict finite negative margin. Sending its tilt to infinity while placing
the threshold halfway across that base gap captures exactly its full
selected fibers, uniformly for the fixed continuous normal. The resulting
margin tends to infinity. Equality base depth=Q is therefore on the
infinite side, as the source emphasizes.

The scalar relation B(w,delta)<=Q iff delta<=r_Q follows with the correct
sign from threshold a.z+u.y-delta. Attainment is necessary at equality
and is supplied above. A negative signed radius does exclude delta=0;
the source does not silently replace it by its positive part at that
stage. The later positive-part obstacle is stated only for positive
parameter values, which handles this distinction correctly.

At a sampled interior mark with positive atomic gap, an attained
nonnegative-margin cap contains the mark. A full own trace would imply
the atomic lower bound and is impossible at mass Q. Its proper own
section therefore supplies local strict decrease of the projection tail.
This justifies the additional strict scalar statement at sampled marks,
without importing it at arbitrary unsampled real bases.

## 3. Boundary and convexity details

At a real fiber-boundary mark, choose a continuous supporting normal.
For the canonical hull, its real-base support height is exactly the
finite concave LP roof of the sampled support heights: maximizing the
linear continuous functional commutes with the finite barycentric hull
description. A finite affine supporting majorant exists even at the
boundary of the base polytope, since the roof is polyhedral. The resulting
ambient supporting cap has zero mixed volume: its continuous normal is
nonzero and each sampled fiber is full dimensional. Its left Q-quantile
lies strictly below that support height, proving r_Q>0 or infinity.

Consequently the convention T_Q=infinity at fiber boundaries agrees with
the CLOSED perspective x^(d+1)/s^d, applied to x=max(r_Q,0) and
s=E^(1/d). The composition inequality has the required directions:
the perspective is increasing in its convex first input and decreasing
in its concave positive second input. Its closed extension at s=0 is
infinite for the strictly positive first input that actually occurs here.
The lsc statement follows as written. Extending by infinity outside the
convex canonical body preserves convexity.

The equivalence of the global sampled sublevel constraint with L<=T_Q
is exact, but does not supply a finite witness set or a Gamma payment.
That limitation is retained in the source.

## 4. Actual plateau calibration

In the binary-square interval example the real fiber at
z=(1/2,1/2) is indeed [-h,1/2+h]. Opposite margin sums are+1/2 and-1/2
(interchanged when reversing the continuous normal), so every nonnegative
buffer cap captures a whole interval. The displayed tilt captures just
one until delta=1/4-h. Beyond that threshold one of the negative-pair
intervals must acquire positive mass in addition to the whole interval,
so the sublevel radius cannot be larger. The left and right quantile
endpoints h and1-h therefore give different margins exactly as printed.
The real-fiber mark is its centroid, so its ordinary interval energy is
its length1/2+2h. This checks the final obstacle formula and its distinction
from the projected superlevel threshold.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
